title: The Envoy
note: He defines this as the nature of those sent to other rulers to make peace or war. One kind frames his own words and equals a minister. The other repeats what he was told and has a quarter less of a minister’s qualities.

couplets.plain: Loving-kindness, birth in a good family, and the qualities rulers desire: these are the qualities of an envoy.
couplets.pm: The marks of an envoy are loving-kindness towards his own kin, birth in a family fit for a minister’s office, and the qualities the caste of rulers desires. The first means he sees that no harm comes to his kin. The second means he has heard from his forebears how envoys act. The third brings foreign rulers under his sway.

links.reason: Loving-kindness comes first in the envoy’s list.
The qualities rulers desire complete the three.

couplets.plain: Loving-kindness, understanding and skill in well-weighed speech: envoys can’t do without these three.
couplets.pm: Loving-kindness for his own ruler, the understanding to know what serves him, and skill in weighing his words before foreign rulers: an envoy can’t do without these three. Weighing means choosing the words they will agree to. “Can’t do without” implies that he needs the other marks of ministers too.

links.reason: Loving-kindness leads the envoy’s three needs.

couplets.plain: To be a master of the books among those who know the books: that is the quality of one who speaks for victory among men of the spear.
couplets.pm: One who goes among foreign rulers and their spears, and says what will win victory for his own ruler, must be a master of statecraft among ministers who know it. “Spear” shows they are given to killing. “Victory” covers both tasks of an envoy. Mastery means being able to expound it before those who only know it.

links.quote: speaks for victory among men of the spear
links.reason: One who speaks for victory among men of the spear is the envoy in all but name.

links.quote: a master of the books among those who know the books

couplets.plain: Let the one who has all three, understanding, presence and well-tested learning, go on this work.
couplets.pm: Natural understanding, a look that pleases the eye, and learning tested with many people many times: let the one who has these together go as envoy to foreign rulers. They are rarely found in one man. They win him esteem, and then the work is easily finished.

links.quote: Let the one who has all three

links.reason: Learning completes the three, after understanding and presence.

couplets.plain: An envoy sums up, drops what is harsh, speaks so that people smile, and brings about good.
couplets.pm: An envoy, with many matters to put to foreign rulers, gathers them under one cause. With unwelcome matters, he drops harsh words and uses sweet ones that gladden. Those who refuse many things agree to one cause, not seeing what follows. Those who refuse the unwelcome agree when gladdened, not seeing the sting. So he brings his ruler good.

links.reason: Lays down how an envoy’s manner of speaking brings about good.
Speaking so that people smile is the third means.
Dropping what is harsh is the second means.

couplets.plain: An envoy is learned, unafraid of a hard stare, speaks so that it goes home, and knows what suits the time.
couplets.pm: An envoy has learned statecraft, says what he came for so that hostile rulers take it in, doesn’t fear their angry gaze, and knows the means that suit the time. Learning shows him the means, and if the time comes when the work must be finished some other way, he must know that too.

links.reason: Not fearing a hard stare is the courage asked of him before a hostile ruler.

links.quote: speaks so that it goes home

couplets.plain: The finest is the one who knows his duty, watches the time, knows the place, thinks it through and then speaks.
couplets.pm: The highest envoy weighs the standing of foreign rulers, of his own ruler and of himself, and acts to fit. He watches for the moment they will listen, chooses a place where his helpers are present, and works out in advance what he will say, their reply and his answer. Sanskrit books rank envoys highest, middle and lowest, so he says “finest”.

links.quote: watches the time, knows the place

couplets.plain: Purity, support and resolve, with truth alongside: these are the marks of one who carries a message.
couplets.pm: One who carries his ruler’s words unchanged to foreign rulers needs four things. Purity from wealth and desire, so he won’t alter them. The support of their ministers, to ease the anger his ruler’s boasts arouse. Resolve, so he won’t drop a word for fear of harm. And truth, so that everyone trusts him.

links.reason: Sets the marks for the one who carries a message.
Resolve is the third of the marks.
Purity opens the list of marks.

couplets.plain: The one who delivers a message to rulers is a man of firm heart, whose mouth lets no scarring word slip.
couplets.pm: The one fit to deliver his ruler’s message to foreign rulers is a man of firmness, who won’t, in fear of harm to himself, let slip even by accident a word that lowers his ruler. Lowering him isn’t the duty of his caste, so such a word is a scar.

links.quote: The one who delivers a message to rulers
links.reason: Fixes on who is fit to carry a message to rulers.
He keeps every scarring word from leaving his mouth.

couplets.plain: An envoy is one who, even if it brings his death, holds nothing back and brings about what is good for his ruler.
couplets.pm: An envoy is one who, even if the words will end his life, doesn’t fall back in fear, but says to foreign rulers just what his ruler told him, to his ruler’s advantage. If death won’t stop him, nothing less needs mentioning.

links.quote: even if it brings his death
links.reason: Holds up the true envoy at the moment of greatest danger.

links.quote: brings about what is good for his ruler
